paper_metadata.title: Effects of different Al contents on mechanical properties and high temperature oxidation resistance of AlxCoCr0.6NiV0.6 high entropy alloy

From SAl0 to SAl4, the matrix of the high-entropy alloys is FCC, and with the precipitation of L12 phase, the compressive yield strength of the high-entropy alloy is significantly increased from 235 MPa to 570 MPa, by about 142 % (Fig. 6a).

From SAl0 to SAl4, the matrix of the high-entropy alloys is FCC, and with the precipitation of L12 phase, the compressive yield strength of the high-entropy alloy is significantly increased from 235 MPa to 570 MPa, by about 142 % (Fig. 6a).
For SAl6, the yield strength is greatly increased to 1.8 GPa, and the fracture plasticity is still greater than 15 %.

Though the work-hardening rates of SAl0 to SAl8, it is proved that SAl4 has the highest work-hardening rate at 22.25 GPa, twice that of SAl0 (Fig. 6c).
When the Al content is 6 wt%, the oxidation rate of the alloy after the whole oxidation cycle is low, which is 0.77 mg⋅cm-2.
Compared with the Al content of 6 wt%, the oxidative weight gain (0.67 mg⋅cm-2) of HEAs did not change significantly when the content of Al in the alloy was 8 wt%.
The yield strength of the high-entropy alloy increased from 235 MPa to 974 MPa, while the oxide layer thickness decreased from 37.5 μm to 8.3 μm, representing a reduction of 77 %.
With an additional increase of Al content to 6 wt%, the thickness of both the oxide layer and oxygen layer is further reduced to 12.2 μm, resulting in an overall thickness reduction of 68 %.
In this study, the expansion of lattice distortion effect in the microstructure confirms the existence of solid solution strengthening.
The grain refinement induced by the heterogeneous structure is the reason for the significant increase in the yield strength of SAl0 to SAl4.

the strengthening mechanism of the alloy after adding Al element can be summarized as follows: ① fcc matrix solid solution strengthening, ② refined crystalline strengthening caused by SRO, ③ and L12 and dual phase strengthening caused by bcc structure.
